he facility is purpose-built for specialist surgery, with multiple theatres and advanced ophthalmic technology, alongside ENT, facial and other surgical specialties.

job.title: Clinical Care Lead
job.description:

  • Strong technology skills and confidence implementing new systems

  • Opportunity to influence clinical standards and business growth

You're a nurse who sees possibilities. You're ambitious, relationship-driven, commercially aware, and passionate about delivering exceptional care. You enjoy building teams, solving problems, and being part of something growing and exciting.

  • Permanent, full-time position

  • Sydney CBD 

  • Hours: 8am–4pm or 9am–5pm

  • Competitive hourly rate of $40–$60 per hour + super, dependent on experience

  • Work directly alongside a Fertility Specialist and experienced clinical team

  • Well-established private practice environment

  • Excellent onboarding, training and ongoing development

  • 4 weeks' buddying and support when you start

  • Opportunity to build on your existing fertility/IVF expertise

About the Role

This is more than a traditional clinical nursing position. You’ll become an important point of contact for patients throughout their fertility journey, combining your clinical knowledge with exceptional communication, coordination and patient care.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing nursing support throughout the fertility treatment journey

  • Coordinating patient care between the Fertility Specialist, patients and wider clinical team

  • Supporting patients through treatment pathways and follow-up

  • Providing education, information and reassurance to patients

  • Managing multiple patients and priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail

  • Building strong and trusted relationships with patients

  • Working autonomously while remaining closely connected to the wider team

  • Contributing to a positive and highly personalised patient experience

  • Using technology and digital systems to support efficient patient coordination

You’ll also have the opportunity to work with a range of technology platforms, with full support and training provided.

About You

To be successful, you’ll have:

  • Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse

  • Previous fertility/IVF nursing experience – essential

  • Experience supporting patients through fertility treatment

  • Strong patient coordination and organisational skills

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

  • High emotional intelligence and a genuinely compassionate approach

  • The ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities

  • Strong attention to detail

  • Confidence working within a specialist/private practice environment

  • Australian working rights

IVF/fertility experience is essential for this position. The successful candidate will need to be confident stepping into a specialist fertility environment and supporting patients from day one.

Why This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to move beyond traditional ward-based nursing and become a key part of a specialist fertility practice where patient relationships, continuity of care and clinical expertise really matter.

You’ll work alongside an experienced team, receive structured support when you join and have the opportunity to continue developing your career within the fertility and reproductive health space.

job.title: Registered Nurse - Rehabilitation | Sydney CBD
job.description:
Registered Nurse – Rehabilitation | Sydney CBD

Are you feeling burnt out in hospital, clinic, or ward-based environments and looking for a role where you can still utilise your clinical knowledge in a more autonomous and varied way?

We are currently exclusively partnering with a leading national workplace rehabilitation provider (award-winning and highly regarded in the industry), expanding within their Same Employer division, supporting injured workers with physical injuries to safely return to their current workplace and employer.

This is an opportunity to step into a Rehabilitation Consultant role where you can continue using your nursing and clinical assessment skills in a more flexible and consultative environment, supporting injured workers back into employment and independence.

You’ll have the freedom to choose your work-from-home and office days, manage your own schedule, and work autonomously within a highly supportive team. Working hours sit between 8am–6pm, with flexibility to manage your day around outcomes rather than rigid time constraints.

What’s on offer
• Permanent full-time and part-time positions available
• Salary $80,000 – $100,000 + super (depending on experience)
• Monthly bonus structure
• Hybrid working model (2 days in office, flexibility across WFH and community visits)
• Extremely structured onboarding and induction program designed to set you up for success
• Laptop and phone provided
• Travel reimbursed (km, tolls, parking)
• Strong career progression pathways including leadership opportunities
• Weekly and monthly training, supervision, and development support

About the role

As a Rehabilitation Consultant, you will play a key role in supporting injured workers through their recovery and helping them safely return to meaningful employment and independence.

You will:
• Manage a portfolio of clients with physical and psychological injuries
• Complete initial assessments to identify barriers impacting recovery and return-to-work outcomes
• Develop tailored return-to-work and rehabilitation plans
• Liaise closely with employers, insurers, treating doctors, and allied health professionals
• Attend medical appointments and workplace visits with clients where required
• Support and guide clients through their recovery journey using strong communication and stakeholder management skills
• Complete case management documentation, reports, and case notes
• Coordinate interventions and facilitate safe, graduated return-to-work outcomes
• Build strong relationships with stakeholders to achieve the best possible outcomes for clients

About you
• General Registration with AHPRA as a Registered Nurse
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
• Ability to work autonomously and manage a varied caseload
• Comfortable with travel and community-based work
• Current driver’s licence and access to a vehicle
• Looking to move into a consultative, outcomes-focused role outside of traditional clinical settings

This is a chance to step away from clinical burnout and into a role where your nursing knowledge, communication skills, and clinical reasoning can still make a genuine impact, while offering greater flexibility, autonomy, and long-term career development.
